spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Understand that the first heavenly human state possessed a far greater fullness of reception and a more powerful completeness of life, and that its states of wisdom were extended and manifold. It was not alone in this; those who proceeded from that first state shared the same largeness of capacity and length of spiritual endurance. But as successive states arose, the power of reception in those who later came forth was reduced, and the continuance of their states was shortened. The order by which good and truth are received had not itself been displaced, nor had the universal framework of arranged knowledges in externals been moved from its fixed service; yet the later human state became weaker and briefer than the earlier state.

This change occurred because the governing determinations that measure and distribute the human state are administered through a sufficient series of ruling agencies set over the ordered arrangement of external knowledges and the higher plane that flows into them. These administrations are distinguished as five successive modes of ruling: the widest mode that comprehends an entire cycle, the mode that divides that cycle into lesser cycles, the mode that determines particular states within those, the mode that defines still more specific variations, and the mode that fixes the least distinguishable changes. These five modes are permanent in the structure of the external and inner planes. Each mode has its own power, and a ruling agency is established over each. One administration presides over the whole cycle, another over the divided cycles, another over the particular states, another over their finer variations, and another over the least moments of change. These rule in order, the higher setting bounds for the lower, and the lower executing within the limits of the higher.

According to these administrations, spiritual life comes forth in human beings and also in their lower affections. Their first emergence is under one or another of these ruling determinations. For this reason these administrations have exercised authority from the first setting in order of spiritual life even to its last state. In the earliest states, the administrations that presided over the widest cycles were dominant. Therefore those who came forth under that governance possessed a more extended continuance of state, and their endurance in wisdom was found to be greater. A long spiritual life is perceived in the first heavenly humanity, and in the truth that proceeded from it, and in those who followed in that early succession.

When the dominance of the administrations over the widest cycles ended, the administrations over the divided cycles came into rule. And because those cycles are shorter than the whole, those who came forth under this governance had a briefer continuance of state. Their endurance was less than the endurance of those who belonged to the earlier governance.

When the governance of the divided cycles was fulfilled, the administrations of particular states received authority after them. And because particular states are briefer than the divided cycles, so also the continuance of those who came forth under them was shorter than the continuance of those who belonged to the governance of the divided cycles. Likewise, those who came forth under the governance of finer variations, and under the least moments of change, had still less continuance; the measure and transmission of their life was narrower than that of the broader administrations.

Consider further how an entire derived humanity could proceed from a single origin of good and a single origin of truth united as one.

The character of the earliest states was that they were richer in wisdom and purer in the form of life, and their continuance was greater. Consequently, what proceeded from them was far more abundant than what proceeds from later states. For a longer time the inward formation of new life remained within the protecting interior, until it was sufficiently organized for outward manifestation. Afterward, within one and the same interior reception, many distinct beginnings could be formed together. At times a full complement of new determinations would come forth from a single interior reception, and at times a complement still more abundant; in other cases less, and in other cases greater. By this abundance the derivations from the first truth-bearing receptacle were multiplied, and from them further derivations. The ultimate plane of life was filled by them alone, because the proceeders from the ancient state differed greatly from those of the later state. The way they received influx and brought it forth into outward life was not like the later way of producing new states in the external human.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strong coherence as a single teaching: an ordered decline in the breadth of governing measures narrows the duration and potency of human spiritual states, followed by an account of how abundant derivations can proceed from a unified origin. Voice and sequence remain consistent; only a few terms (“houses/positions,” “conduit”) required generalized spiritual phrasing.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential opening: a functional question about why early humanity was larger/longer-lived though the cosmic order (stars/zodiac) remains fixed. No textual seam or foreign voice is required to make the narrative work.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by observable function and comparison: “Adam is mighty in his stature… his years are many… these people who are born today, their stature has been diminished… even their years are lessened.” The rhetorical problem is framed against stable cosmology: “the stars and signs of the zodiac continue in their positions.” The spiritual reading reports “Notes: Clean” and that it “OPENS… posing the question of decline,” which matches the paragraph’s own interrogative structure (“Also, why…?”).

findings.diagnosis: Insertion of administrative-astrological taxonomy into an otherwise functional inquiry. The paragraph shifts from ‘why decline?’ to a fivefold bureaucracy of ‘masters’ and ranked authority, with named offices (year/month/day/hour/moment) and “houses/positions.” This is governance-by-jurisdiction, not correspondence-by-function. It still connects loosely to the theme (time-measures), but the teaching mode changes abruptly and forces the spiritual reading into abstraction.
findings.evidence: The paragraph is dominated by appointment and rank: “five types of authorities and leaders appointed… They have names… the first name is the year… second… month… third… day… fourth… hour… fifth… moment.” Then territorial/structural administration: “five positions… five houses… five powers… made masters over them… The master of the year exists… In turn one is above his companion.” The Stage 3a reader explicitly signals strain: “The ‘five houses/positions’ required a generalized rendering as stable structural modes,” i.e., the spiritual sense does not arise naturally from function but is reconstructed to accommodate a governmental list. That is the hallmark of an inserted administrative layer.
findings.scope: “They increased, have turned, and diminished; because there are five types of authorities and leaders appointed in the sphere of zodiacal signs, and the heavens above it. They have names they are ca[lled] by: the first name is the year; the sec[on]d is the month; the third is the day; the fou[rth] is the hour; the fifth is the moment. Now, these five positions, and these five houses, exist in the sphere and the heavens. These places have five powers, and they are made masters over them. The master of the year exists; the master of the month exists; the master of the day exists; the master of the hour exists; the master of the moment exists. In turn one is above his companion; and in turn the one above is made the master over the one below him.”

findings.diagnosis: Mixed paragraph: it begins in administrative voice (authority-from-beginning, powers reigning), but then reattaches to the chapter’s functional question about lifespan in early generations. The administrative framing appears to be the continuation of ¶3’s inserted system; the Adam/Sethel application is the substrate’s intended anchor.
findings.evidence: Administrative governance continues: “these powers have received authority since the beginning of creation till the end of the world… the powers who were masters over the years reigned.” This is explicitly jurisdictional (“received authority,” “masters,” “reigned”). Yet the paragraph’s second half returns to the chapter’s original problem: “Therefore… their years were found to be greater… long life span in the generation of Adam, and [tha]t of Sethel his son.” The spiritual reading treats it as smooth (“CONTINUES by applying the ruling modes”), but that smoothness depends on accepting ¶3’s bureaucratic scheme; without ¶3, the administrative half reads like a foreign explanatory apparatus attached to an otherwise simple ‘early state had longer life’ observation.
findings.scope: “And, thus, these powers have received authority since the beginning of creation till the end of the world. Now, in the beginning of the generations the powers who were masters over the years reigned.”

findings.diagnosis: Continuation of the same administrative time-bureaucracy (year→month→day→hour/moment) used to explain diminishing lifespans. The sequence is internally consistent, but it remains governance-by-successive administrations rather than correspondential teaching by function. ¶6 also shows a minor textual/lexical difficulty (“conduit”), suggesting either translation friction or corruption in this layer.
findings.evidence: Pure administrative succession: “After they ceased to reign… the powers who are masters over the months… reigned” (¶5); “the powers of the days received authority after them” (¶6); then “offspring… born in the hours, and of the moments.” The reader notes strain at a key word: “ ‘Conduit’ forced a rendering… exact nuance uncertain,” which is consistent with a technical or damaged term in a schematic overlay. The logic ‘shorter unit → shorter lifespan’ works, but it works as an imposed administrative measurement system rather than an organic correspondence arising from bodily/cosmic function.
findings.scope: Annotate ¶5–¶6 as an administrative schematization (successive ‘masters’ of temporal units governing lifespans), including the problematic term “Their {conduit} is less…”, rather than treating it as pure correspondential substrate.

findings.diagnosis: Clean seam and genuine topic-shift marker, not an insertion: the text openly signals a new question (generation from one pair). This is a normal didactic transition and does not introduce alien administrative lists.
findings.evidence: The paragraph is a direct rhetorical pivot: “Now, can you recount to me this other (matter): By what sort of birth was the entire offspring… made from one man and one woman…?” The spiritual reading likewise notes “SHIFTS… to the question of spiritual propagation,” and reports “Notes: Clean.” No governance/jurisdiction language appears; it’s inquiry into generative process.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential generative teaching using embodied process (gestation, multiple births) as the functional basis for explaining early abundance and later reduction. No narrative break; the bodily imagery is integral rather than an administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: The teaching proceeds by functional natural analogy: “richer in their light and purer in stature… spending a longer time [forming] in the womb… brought forth a number in a single womb… times five… times six… The earth was filled…” This is exactly correspondence-by-function: longer formation → greater abundance; multiple births → multiplication/filling. The reader confirms the only issue is interpretive translation pressure, not incoherence: “bodily language… required translation into interior formation… overall flow remains coherent.” That is accommodation, not a textual seam.

textual_criticism.summary: 6 findings. The chapter has a strong correspondential substrate in ¶2 and ¶9–¶10 (decline in human vitality; then embodied generation/abundance). The major disruption is an administrative-astrological fivefold ‘masters’ taxonomy in ¶3, which forces generalized spiritual paraphrase; excision is recommended for all of ¶3. ¶4 is mixed; excise the brief governance framing that depends on ¶3, while retaining the Adam/Sethel lifespan application. ¶5–¶6 form a coherent administrative overlay sequence; recommend annotation (do not carve it up), with a note on the lexical difficulty ‘conduit’.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Now, no[te] that Adam is mighty in his stature, and great is his size. Even his years are many! He spent many years living in the world. And he is not the only one we have found to be mighty; but all the others who were begotten in his generation, many are their years too. Still, these people who are born today, their stature has been diminished in power; even their years are lessened. Also, why is the birth today, of [the]y who are born, altered compared with that of these first [ones, and they did not change from] place to place? See, even the stars and signs of the zodiac continue in their positions. Why now have the age and the years of these last ones diminished, and he has also become smaller, compared to these ancient ones who belong to these first generations?
They increased, have turned, and diminished.

So, mankind is begotten, and [the ani]mals. They are born in these powers. Therefore, because of this, the offspring born in their generations and their lifetime: their years were found to be greater. They attain a long life span in the generation of Adam, and [tha]t of Sethel his son, and that of the ones who came after him.

After they ceased to reign, namely the powers who are masters over the years; the powers who are masters over the months themselves reigned. Like the months, for they are less than the years; again this [is] also the case with the offspring w[ho were] born in them. Their life span is less [than the life span of the ones born] in the generation of the powers who master the years!

When the authority of the powers who master the months was completed; the powers of the days received authority after them. Therefore, like the days, for they are less than the months, this also is the case with the offspring who were born in them. Their life span is less than the life span of the ones born in the powers who are masters over the months. Again, even so the offspring who were born in the hours, and of the moments. Their {conduit} is less than that of the months and the days.
Now, can you recount to me this other (matter): By what sort of birth was the entire offspring of mankind made from one man and one woman, Adam and Eve?

For the manner of these first generations is that they are richer in their light and purer in stature. Even their years are greater. Thus, again, even their offspring is much more than the offspring of this tim[e]. They were spending a longer time [forming] in [the w]omb of their mother. Afterwards, they [brought forth] a number in a single womb. There are times five were brought forth from a single womb, and times six were brought forth from [a] single womb! There are some lesser than this; again, some greater than this. Indeed, because of this the offspring of Eve multiplied, and of her children. The earth was filled by reason of them alone; because the offspring from the generation of the people of old, who they bore into the world, differ greatly from those of today. Their conception and their birth is not like latter births, brought forth nowadays from the woman's uterus.

changes_summary: Applied excisions per the critic’s recommendations: (1) Finding 2 (¶3) excise—removed the administrative-astrological fivefold ‘masters’ taxonomy; retained only the opening clause so the paragraph remains grammatical and coherent. (2) Finding 3 (¶4) excise—removed the specified governance framing (“And, thus, these powers have received authority… reigned”), keeping the Adam/Sethel lifespan application. No other paragraphs were altered; Findings 1, 5, 6 recommended none, and Finding 4 recommended annotation only (no textual change).
